summary: The numerical repairs pass the complete historical and policy smoke tests. The 32-start search returned 27 valid histories, three market-convergence failures and two timeouts. None improved the retained starting point. No differential-evolution or polishing round fit the remaining budget. This is a verified experiment with a limited search, not a fully optimized replacement calibration. Final repetitions, local sensitivity calculations and 2023–2063 policy paths are running.
interpretation: The main fit problem is the parent/nonparent ownership gap: the model produces 0.44 percentage points against a 16.77-point target, contributing 379.21 of the 450.71 loss. First-birth rooms rise by 0.365 against a 0.720 target, and births occur too early. Smaller-shock starts can improve ownership differences but fit childlessness and birth timing much worse. Tenure nests impose a fertility scale λκ no larger than tenure scale κ. Other parameters also vary across the starts, so this pattern is not an optimized frontier or proof that simultaneous choice cannot fit the data.
outstanding: The chosen nesting restriction remains experimental. The first-child room-floor jump has an upper search bound of 2 rooms, compared with 0.5 in the retained benchmark. Market-convergence failures and the time-limited search restrict the conclusions. High-income wealth reaches the upper plotted boundary; final sensitivity and policy evidence remain to be certified. The existing production calibration is retained.
